expenditures.anchor: Form B's own printed 'Total Expenditures: (to line 2 of report): 17,474 00' = 17,474.00, which is also the cover's line-2 Totals-for-THIS-REPORT cell
expenditures.detail: 13 Form B rows sum to 17,766.00 against the filer's printed schedule total of 17,474.00 - a FILER-ARITHMETIC delta of +292.00, retained verbatim and never nudged. Traced as far as the document allows: this sheet prints NO per-page subtotal (only the grand total), so there is no sub-anchor to localize the error against; instead every one of the 13 amount cells was re-read on a tight --value crop at 900 dpi and the five least certain again at 1,200-2,400 dpi (1,050 / 2,500 / 1,320 / 2,000 / 126 / 1,320 / 2,500 / 200 / 250 / 1,200 / 2,800 / 1,000 / 1,500), and no single row, and no pair of rows, differs from the transcription by 292.00 - so the difference is the filer's addition, not a mis-read cell and not a missing row (the sheet's 13 filled rows were counted against the printed grid: 13 dates, 13 payees, 13 amounts, rows 14+ blank). The cover is internally consistent AT 17,474.00 (21,218.46 last + 17,474.00 this = 38,692.46 cumulative, exactly as printed), which is why the printed total, not the row sum, is named as the anchor. Both in-kind conventions were tested and neither closes: no row on this schedule is labelled in-kind, so monetary-only and monetary-plus-in-kind are the same 17,766.00. Period-scoped behind a cumulative cover (last report 21,218.46 carried from the prior cycle's account), i.e. this would be period-exact but for the 292.00.

41.measure_note: ROTATED landscape sheet: the sheet's top edge is the image's LEFT edge, so rows advance LEFT-TO-RIGHT (axis x) and the printed ROW rules are the page's VERTICAL rules. rowbands.py's own vertical pass returns almost nothing here because it measures verticals over the whole h-rule span at 60% coverage; re-detected over the table's y-window (6-95 pct) at 30-45% coverage the grid comes out clean and regular: rules at 6.74 (binding bar), 9.06 (table border), 12.24 (label column), 15.26 (end of the grey shaded strip) and then a constant 3.06-3.21 pct pitch to 87.0. The 23 DATA bands stored here start at 15.26 - the header/label column and the shaded strip are TRIMMED OUT, so row N resolves to rows[N-1]. COLUMN bands are the horizontal rules re-detected over x=15-88 at 90% coverage: 5.5 / 16.23 / 58.43 / 88.61 / 96.75 = Amount | Address | Name of Contributor | Date; `cell` is the AMOUNT band [5.5,16.23], verified by cropping it and getting figures, not names. INDEXING PROOF (addendum A3): pct:15.26,5.50,3.21,10.73@p41 renders '$5(slashed0)(slashed0)-' = the 500.00 recorded for row 1, and pct:37.41,5.50,3.18,10.73@p41 renders '$5(slashed0)(slashed0)' = the 500.00 recorded for row 8 (NWHBA), with row 2's crop rendering the disputed '$1(slashed0)(slashed0)' and row 7's the '$5,(slashed0)(slashed0)(slashed0)-' - neighbours differ, so the band list is not off by one.

42.measure_note: Same rotated landscape geometry as p41 but a DIFFERENT origin - do not copy p41's bands onto it. Vertical (row) rules re-detected over y=6-95 pct at 30% coverage: 6.62 binding bar, 9.0 table border, 12.59/13.06 label column, then the grey shaded strip [13.06,16.09] AND a further empty printed band [16.09,19.18] before the first data row; a first attempt that started the data at 16.09 pointed every row one early and was caught by the crop proof, which is exactly the defect addendum A2 describes. The 23 DATA bands stored here therefore start at 19.18, constant 3.03-3.18 pct pitch to 90.0. COLUMN bands are the horizontal rules over x=15-88 at 90% coverage: 4.32 / 15.05 / 33.91 / 44.59 / 90.02 / 98.07 = Amount | Purpose of Expenditure | City | Person or Organization | Date of Expenditure; `cell` is the AMOUNT band [4.32,15.05]. INDEXING PROOF (addendum A3): pct:19.18,4.32,3.03,10.73@p42 renders '$1,(slashed0)5(slashed0)' = the 1,050.00 recorded for row 1 (Loyal Perch Media), and pct:56.18,4.32,3.08,10.73@p42 renders '$1,5(slashed0)(slashed0)' = the 1,500.00 recorded for row 13 (DIC Inc.).

contributions.note: AMOUNT DECIDED BY THE DOCUMENT'S OWN ARITHMETIC, not by the glyph. At 1600 dpi the cell reads as '$1' followed by what could be two or three slashed-zero loops and the filer's terminal flourish; there is NO comma, whereas every four-figure amount this filer wrote on both schedules ($1,050 / $1,320 / $2,500 / $5,000 / $9,000 / $4,000) carries one. With 100 here the eight rows sum to 24,300.00, which is EXACTLY the schedule's own printed 'Total Contributions: (to line 1 of report)' AND the cover's line-1 Totals-for-This-Report cell; with 1,000 nothing on the document closes. Per the GOTCHAS Rhodes ruling (escalation resolves legibility, never truth - the schedule's sum decides), 100.00 is recorded, flagged for review.

notes: James H. 'Jim' Harvey, Weber County Commission Seat C, 2024 cycle, October 8 pre-election report (only that box ticked), signed 04 Oct. 2024.
